# ShopBoard — Day 3 AI Code Review Log (`ai-products.ts` Audit)

This document records the technical code review of the AI-generated TypeScript module from the CorePro Day 3 Review Lab (`https://shopboard-api.vercel.app/review-lab` — `ai-products.ts`) and explains how each identified issue is prevented in ShopBoard's Day 3 TypeScript and API architecture.

---

## Reference Code Audited (`ai-products.ts`)

```ts
// ai-products.ts — generated by an AI assistant when asked:
// "Write a TypeScript module that fetches products from our API and renders them."

const API = "https://shopboard-api.vercel.app";

export async function loadAndRenderProducts(containerSelector: string) {
  const res = await fetch(`${API}/api/products`);
  const data = (await res.json()) as any; // [1]

  const container = document.querySelector(containerSelector)!; // [2]
  container.innerHTML = "";

  for (const item of data.items) {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.className = "product-card";
    // Price comes back from the API in cents — e.g. 2999 = $29.99
    card.innerHTML = `
      <h3>${item.title}</h3>
      <p class="category">${item.category}</p>
      <p class="price">$${item.price}</p>
      <button data-id="${item.id}">Add to cart</button>
    `;
    container.appendChild(card);

    card.querySelector("button")!.addEventListener("click", () => {
      // [3]
      const saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("cart") || "[]");
      saved.push({ id: item.id, qty: 1 });
      localStorage.setItem("cart", JSON.stringify(saved));
    });
  }
}
```

---

## Issue 1: Silent Type Erasure via `as any` (`const data = (await res.json()) as any`)

- **Category:** TypeScript Type Safety & Runtime Validation
- **Where it occurs:** Line 8 (`const data = (await res.json()) as any;`)
- **What is wrong:** Casting the parsed JSON response to `any` completely disables the TypeScript compiler for `data` and every property accessed on `item` inside the loop. TypeScript cannot warn that `item.category` and `item.price` do not exist on the real API payload (`category_name` and `price_cents`). Furthermore, if the API returns an unexpected JSON shape (such as `{ error: "..." }` or `null`), `for (const item of data.items)` throws an unhandled `TypeError: data.items is not iterable`.
- **Real-user impact:** Any backend schema change or malformed response crashes the product catalog at runtime with an uncaught exception, leaving the user staring at a blank product section.
- **How ShopBoard fixes it:**
  - `src/shared/api/client.ts` types raw JSON as `unknown` (`const rawData: unknown = await res.json()`) and requires a runtime validator `(raw: unknown) => T`.
  - `src/modules/products/products.api.ts` defines explicit wire interfaces (`ApiProduct`, `ApiProductList`) and validates every field at runtime using `isApiProduct()`, `parseApiProduct()`, and `parseApiProductList()` without a single `any` or `as` assertion.

---

## Issue 2: Missing `res.ok` Check & Missing Async UI States (Loading, Error, Empty, Retry)

- **Category:** Async Network Error Handling & UX Resilience
- **Where it occurs:** Lines 7–8 (`const res = await fetch(...); const data = await res.json();`)
- **What is wrong:** `fetch()` only rejects on network-level failures (such as DNS failure or offline mode); it resolves normally on HTTP `404` and `500` responses. The AI-generated function never checks `if (!res.ok)`, never wraps the request in error handling, shows no loading indicator while the request is in flight, shows no empty state if `data.items` is `[]`, and provides no Retry button if the request fails.
- **Real-user impact:** On a slow connection, the user sees nothing while waiting. On a `500` server error, the app attempts to iterate `data.items` on an error JSON payload (`{ error: "Simulated 500 error..." }`), throwing an uncaught `TypeError` with no error message and no way for the user to retry without refreshing the entire browser tab.
- **How ShopBoard fixes it:**
  - `src/shared/api/client.ts` checks `if (!res.ok)` and throws a typed `ApiError(res.status, message)`.
  - `src/modules/products/products.types.ts` models the catalog lifecycle as an explicit discriminated union (`LoadState`: `loading`, `error`, `success`).
  - `src/modules/products/products.ui.ts` (`renderCatalogState()`) renders dedicated views for Loading, Error (with a working `#retry-fetch-btn` "Try Again" button), Empty API response (`.catalog-state-empty-api`), and Empty Search/Filter results (`.catalog-state-empty-filter`), accompanied by an error toast via `showToast(message, "error")`.

---

## Issue 3: Unmapped Wire Format Fields (`item.category` & `item.price` Instead of `category_name` & `price_cents`)

- **Category:** API Wire Format vs. Internal Domain Model
- **Where it occurs:** Lines 17–18 (`<p class="category">${item.category}</p>`, `<p class="price">$${item.price}</p>`)
- **What is wrong:** Despite its own code comment noting that prices come back in cents, the AI-generated code reads `item.category` and `item.price` directly from the raw API object. However, the real `https://shopboard-api.vercel.app/api/products` endpoint returns `category_name` (e.g., `"Bags"`) and `price_cents` (e.g., `8900`). Even if it read `item.price_cents` directly in the UI, rendering `$8900` instead of `$89` would display prices 100x too high.
- **Real-user impact:** Every product card displays `undefined` for its category and `$undefined` for its price (or `$8900` if `price_cents` leaks into the UI), making the storefront unusable.
- **How ShopBoard fixes it:**
  - `src/modules/products/products.api.ts` strictly separates `ApiProduct` (wire format with `title`, `category_name`, `price_cents`, `in_stock`) from `Product` (internal domain model with `name`, `category`, `price` in dollars, `inStock`).
  - `toProduct(api: ApiProduct): Product` is the single boundary where `price_cents` is divided by `100` (`Math.round(api.price_cents) / 100`) and fields are normalized. No UI or logic module ever touches `price_cents`.

---

## Issue 4: Non-Null Assertions (`!`) on DOM Queries (`document.querySelector(...)!`)

- **Category:** DOM Null Safety
- **Where it occurs:** Line 10 (`const container = document.querySelector(containerSelector)!;`) and Line 23 (`card.querySelector("button")!.addEventListener(...)`)
- **What is wrong:** Using the TypeScript non-null assertion operator (`!`) silences the compiler's `Element | null` check without verifying that the element actually exists in the DOM. If `containerSelector` has a typo or the element is absent on the current page, `container.innerHTML = ""` immediately throws `TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting 'innerHTML')`.
- **Real-user impact:** Any missing DOM node crashes the script during initialization and prevents the rest of the page's interactive features from mounting.
- **How ShopBoard fixes it:**
  - Non-null assertions (`!`) are banned across `src/**/*.ts`.
  - Every DOM query in `src/modules/products/products.ui.ts`, `src/modules/cart/cart.ui.ts`, `src/shared/ui/toast.ts`, and `src/ui.ts` is checked explicitly (`if (!container) return;` or `if (el instanceof HTMLElement)`).

---

## Issue 5: Architectural Violation, XSS Injection, Unsafe `localStorage`, and Per-Card Listener Duplication

- **Category:** Modular Architecture, Event Delegation, Storage Safety, and Security
- **Where it occurs:** Lines 6–28 of `ai-products.ts`
- **What is wrong:**
  1. **God-function mixing concerns:** A single function performs `fetch()`, DOM querying, HTML string injection, event binding, and direct `localStorage` mutation.
  2. **XSS vulnerability:** `item.title` and `item.category` from an external API are interpolated directly into `card.innerHTML` without HTML escaping.
  3. **Per-card listener attachment & broken cart logic:** A separate click listener is attached to every button inside the render loop, and clicking "Add to cart" blindly pushes `{ id: item.id, qty: 1 }` into `localStorage` without deduplicating existing items, without wrapping `JSON.parse` in `try...catch`, and without updating any cart UI or showing user feedback.
- **Real-user impact:** Clicking "Add to cart" twice creates duplicate rows instead of incrementing quantity to 2, corrupted `localStorage` data crashes the click handler, and the user receives zero visual confirmation that an item was added.
- **How ShopBoard fixes it:**
  - Concerns are cleanly separated across `src/shared/api/client.ts` (HTTP), `src/modules/products/products.api.ts` (validation & mapping), `src/modules/products/products.logic.ts` (pure filtering/sorting), `src/modules/cart/cart.state.ts` (defensive `try...catch` storage sync + deduplicated quantity increment), and `src/modules/products/products.ui.ts` (escaped HTML rendering + single delegated listener on `#products-grid` + `showToast()` notification).
